entry.title: The problem was never intelligence, it was continuity.
entry.summary: Building an AI Operating Layer Somewhere along the way I realized I had been asking the wrong question. It seemed obvious. If the models kept getting smarter, everything else would fall into place. None of that matters if the next conversation has to start over. Think about that for a second. Then a new model jumps in. And everyone starts rebuilding the same understanding all over again. That felt crazy to me. I thought memory was the answer. Those ideas help, but they don't solve the deeper problem. Memory stores information. That was the turning point. I stopped thinking about memory and started thinking about continuity. What if the important thing wasn't remembering everything? That single question quietly changed the architecture. That has led us into knowledge models, governed context, project reconstruction, and architectural boundaries. Some of those ideas will survive. That's okay. Where I am today I think the harder problem is making sure understanding survives. Maybe every project gets a little wiser than the last. But I think that's a question worth chasing.
